title: What AI tools do you use for coding? And how?
author: LeDilu
selftext:
I’ve been using ChatGPT for quite a while now, but lately there are so many new things popping up like Copilot agents, Codex, and other LLMs. I’m curious what others are using them for when it comes to actual game code, especially in Unity or Godot.

I’ve tried using agents in VS Code for other projects like APIs and tools, and they worked surprisingly well there. But when it comes to game dev connected to an engine, it didn’t seem to perform as well.

comments.author: Disposable110
comments.body: Roocode + Gemini or free local Kimi K2.

replies.author: Disposable110
replies.body: Minimax M2 is likely going to make local code LLM accessible to everyone with a potato, too.

replies.author: ianxplosion-
replies.body: I made the mistake of using Unreal, I can’t trust anybody but the big dogs until I’m able to sit down, scrape the piss out of the internet and try and train a local model, because Epic is cold piss when it comes to documentation

comments.author: Denaton_
comments.body: Codex, i create an empty repo to see how far i can push it.

comments.author: aastle
comments.body: In Unity 6, visual studio with copilot.  AUTocomplete now features copilot suggestions.

comments.author: alokin_09
comments.body: I've been using Kilo Code for the last few months. What's been killing it for me are the different modes for different tasks - architecture, coding, and debug. Been helping their team out on some projects and actually saw people using it for game dev too. Not sure what your experience has been with it, or if you've tried it yet, but I'd suggest you try it out.

replies.author: Silly-Heat-1229
replies.body: I'm using Kilo as well, it's pretty solid!

comments.author: PoppaBigMac
comments.body:
Depends on what I am trying to code. ChatGPT is the worst for most coding, but I’ll still use it for menial tasks.

Lovable is a lot better for regular coding stuff.
MakkoAI is what I use for making games and animations

comments.author: Upper_Avocado_8202
comments.body:
For coding a game im using [Makko.ai](http://Makko.ai) to vibe code, it also refactors pretty well.   
Can push/pull from and to github as well. 

Full disclosure Im one of the co founders along with some friends.

comments.author: Josvdw
comments.body:
I work with Unity daily.

I think Cline in VSCode has worked best for me (compared to Cursor, Claude Code and Augment Code).

If you want to go one level up, you can connect the Unity MCP with Cline to execute tasks for you in Unity. [https://github.com/CoplayDev/unity-mcp](https://github.com/CoplayDev/unity-mcp)

Then the ultimate if you're making games is Coplay. It's an AI code generator and Unity agent that sits inside the Unity game engine. But it's not free. [https://www.coplay.dev/](https://www.coplay.dev/)

comments.author: odragora
comments.body:
When Cursor offered a free week of GPT-5, I was super impressed with using it in Godot. It one-shoted relatively complex tasks such as map generation using Voronoi, and it could generate and edit .tscn scene files so I didn't even have to switch to Godot editor much.

Not sure if the model is still that good or OpenAI have quietly replaced it with a stupid quantized version, which is very possible judging by the sudden decline of Codex coding quality some time after release.

comments.author: Visible-Key-1320
comments.body: I'm currently doing a game project in Ren'Py, and have found that most models are very bad at Ren'Py, maybe because it's so niche. But I actually get the best results from DeepSeek and Google Search AI (but not Gemini for some reason).

comments.author: je386
comments.body:
Copilot coding agent is good at code, okay at UI, bad at creating images/icons.

If you use copilot coding agent, some hints:  
* use .github/copilot-instructions.md and just tell the agent what it should not so and what it should do instead and that it should update the copilot instruction file accordingly.  
* adjust the firewall allowlist to allow relevant sources and then give the URLs to these respources when you write the task/issue  
* write the tasks/issues as if a human developer would have to do it, write small and good defined tasks that are understandable.  
* while the agent is working, you can log on to the session and then it is basically pair programming. The agent tells its thoughts and you can step in and tell when it is running in the wrong direction

comments.author: Admirable_Gazelle453
comments.body: Game dev seems harder for AI since engine context matters a lot, so I’m curious if you’ve tried using tools like Cursor with full project indexing or just chat-based ones, and for simpler parts like landing pages some still use something like Horizons as a more affordable option using the vibecodersnest discount code
